semantic.justification: Original wrapper owns the actual CalendarImpl service and Gregorian 1970 epoch, forwards UTC/local date-time and pending field/validity queries, loads explicit/default calendars with the original optional UTC flag, and catches only actual UNO Exceptions with original empty/zero/false defaults. Calendar names come from the loaded provider, with source genitive-to-month and partitive-to-genitive fallback; returned strings retain independent ownership. setGregorianDateTime performs tools DateTime subtraction without selecting a different calendar. Unconsumed display/native-number methods, full UNO compound ABI, native service-manager registration/refcount/concurrency and final formatter/column/CSV integration remain unverified. B8TCAE adds real CalendarWrapper/CalendarImpl integration over registered providers and pinned locale resources: pre-load UNO defaults, UTC forwarding, invalid field indices, failed-ID rollback, locale reload on the same calendar/timezone cache key, independent grammatical name owners, Hanja success and hanja_yoil resource rejection. Source en_US calendar order includes Gregorian and Jewish. Three200000-unit Locale field cases reproduced a JavaScript argument-spread RangeError; LocaleData field lookup now reuses the existing counted-UTF16 text bridge, preserving every input unit and existing direct/language/en_US fallback. No input cap, resource mutation, service replacement or full native UNO-wrapper ABI claim is introduced. Both convenience service loads and actual FormatElement Sequence ownership are checked; a copied General string retains its real sole logical reference after Sequence destruction. Coverage policy and semantic statuses remain unchanged. B8TCAE checks18 real wrapper forwarding operations under failure of the original RTL allocation slot. Actual unloaded CalendarImpl error messages and calendar-name materialization produce the existing checked SAL Error, which propagates through the UNO Exception filter. The allocator is restored before assertions and normal provider defaults are rechecked. Independent6-case low-level native allocation evidence does not establish high-level native Calendar OOM results, C++ exception behavior, physical recovery or full UNO ABI parity.
